questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could learn about another language and that I could learn about myths, where Ireland was ideal, as it has a rich history, and they still try to keep the Irish language alive. I also wanted to go to a place, where there was a lot of focus on the international students with a lot of activities and opportunities to meet other people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received a folder with a lot of information from UCC, and they also had a guide on their website, so I found it very helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I was informed that there would be three days of orientation, but it was only two days and each lasted two hours each, which I found very disappointing, as I think it could have been more helpful if there was also focus on the social part and getting to know other people. 
There was also a lot of information during the orientation, which of course was necessary, but it was a lot and a bit confusing, as parts of it weren't relevant for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was extremely difficult and very expensive. A lot of the student accommodations didn't take students for only one semester, so I just had to take the first that actually accepted one semester students. I also received the link to the housing page from the university later than others, and since it was first come, first serve, I couldn't find anything through that.
I won't recommend the place I stayed (BottleWorks), as it was way to expensive, and I didn't find the staff helpful at all. It was however close to the university and I did have my own room and bathroom, but it lacked in a lot of areas.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Although, it sounds rough, I think the most important thing is to accept that it is going to be expensive and it is not going to be optimal. Especially with the prices, because I spent a lot of time trying to find something cheaper, but I just had to accept my housing place, as I needed a place to stay. So from the beginning be aware that it is expensive, and start looking very early; I looked a bit later, so that was also an issue.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think the registration proces was very easy, although it was a bit stressful for me, as I am use to choosing my subjects very early, and here you had access two weeks before school starts, and you might not even get your subjects approved before the course starts. They had tried a new system, where you logged in and then you could choose your subjects through the portal. You could see through the portal whether or not your subjects had been approved by UCC, so you could navigate in it yourself. I did however find it very confusing at first that UCC has divided their subjects into visiting students and non-visiting students. My biggest problem with registration was actually my own home university, as they would only accept classes for master, and it was my job to proof it, but UCC didn't offer any information about this. That was extremely stressful and luckily they accepted the subjects in the end

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could stop by the international office, there was orientation, where they guided us through the proces very thoroughly and you had access to the module book

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very succesful, as I luckily got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get stressed out about the very late proces. They also allow students to change subjects within the first two weeks, if it didn't fit you, and you shouldn't be scared to do it. I didn't do it, because I had had so much trouble with my own university that I didn't want to go through that again, but I think it would have been worth it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only had one MA class, the rest were BA classes. The level of the MA class was too difficult, while almost all the others were a fitting level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The exams were by hand without notes, so the exams weren't as extensive as at UCPH, as we couldn't truly investigate subjects for the exams, as the focus was on remembering. However, I did also like having this focus, as it made me look at the subjects in a different way, since I really had to know the stories in order to remember them for the exam, and not "just" analyze them. So I think it was useful to try having that focus on the exam, but I do however like at UCPH that focus is on learning the deeper meaning

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MA class: Livy, BA classes: Greek Mythology, Early Irish I, Celtic Saints, Mabinogi: Legends of Medieval Wales and The Roots of the Arthurian Legend

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend Early Irish I, Mabinogi: Legends of Medieval Wales and the Roots of the Arthurian Legend, as they teachers were very good communicators, and they helped you truly understand.
Early Irish: I would recommend this subject, as Irish is a beautiful and unique language, and this course lets you learn the overall aspects of Irish without going into too many confusing details.
Mabinogi: I had never heard about the collection of stories before, but it was incredible. The Mabinogi draws on earlier legends, both Irish and Welsh and from a common origin, and with this course you get to understand how the myths are intertwined and understand which parts can determine if it is a loan or inherited
Arthur: I didn't know Arthur had Welsh origin before I took this class, and this class very thoroughly goes through all the parts that can be traced back, and why we can see that it is traced back, and how the story has changed into the story we know today

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't really experience any unexpected costs. UCC helps you understand the potential expenses beforehand, and I can't think of anything that I suddenly had to spend my money on unexpectedly

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was surprised how cheap groceries were compared to Danish prices. The housing prices were absolutely more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They had almost everything I would say. And the great thing here is that you can just show up for the events that the societies have, and every week on Instagram they would post all the events that were happening.
One critique is that as an exchange student for only one semester you couldn't engage further than that, and I think it would have helped me get to know more local people, if I could interact with them through for example planning an event or helping set up

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Book Club with the Literature Society, as it was a very cozy and chill event and an easy way to interact with others, as you have a focus point, I would also recommend performances in the hall at UCC, as they were really fun (fx seeing an ABBA cover band), and I would also recommend booking tours (either through the international office or by the international group), as it was a great way to get to see Ireland

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Experience the nature of Ireland or go see the castles, and book a lot of tours in the beginning of the semester, before you get too busy withy exams. I went to West Cork and Northern Ireland, but I would have loved to see even more nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy. People are very friendly, and I think you can learn a lot from just walking around the city and experiencing how people are behaving. UCC has a lot of international students, and that makes it a bit more difficult adjusting to the local culture, as you need to get away from the university in order to actually experience the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I unfortunately don't, as I didn't socialize with that many local students. I did chat with some at the society events, so I think my tip would be to go to the society events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really find any parts particularly challenging, as I found the people of Cork so friendly. Sometimes the accent was a bit challenging, but I didn't meet a lot of people with a heavy accent

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the friendliness like thanking the bus driver when you leave the bus, everyone saying thank you to almost anything, for example when you leave a store you thank the store owner.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get a leap card (a bus card), as it gives you discount on bus drives - and use it to go see the nature
An advice I could have used is relax, as I am use to at UCPH that we have to things done quickly with deadlines, and it stressed me out a lot that the subjects were maybe approved when school started, but it is the same for everyone, so really relax
Look into housing as early as possible. I think I started looking in the middle of March, and it was way too late

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: That both UCC international office and UCC societies uses Instagram a lot for information, so go in and follow them. And I wasn't aware until late that there was a WhatsApp group with a lot of helpful information, so be on the lookout for the link too

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the exchange experience was diving completely into another culture. I think it is amazing how much you learn by actually living in another country and not just visiting. I think some of the most rewarding aspects have been just walking around in the city, going to the local pubs and just embracing the culture and noticing the small things that people do differently.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was not overcoming the part of me that was scared of socializing and scared of not making any friends. It really helped that I made myself go to so many events in September, so it quickly became easier, and I did make some great friends. But that is the good thing about interacting with the other international students, as they are all in the same boat.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
